title: Console (ops-only): surface incident type + owner; define CS-safe visibility for comms
creator: Rachel Kim
project: Reliability Program: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
description:
## Context
As part of the Reliability Program, we’re making `incident_type` + `incident_subtype` required fields (incident-bot + reporting). We also now have an owner mapping (type/subtype -> primary owner team + escalation channel + runbook links) managed via control plane config.

Console is currently missing these fields in the internal ops views, which makes it hard to:
- quickly route triage to the correct owning team during an incident
- do follow-the-sun handoffs with consistent classification
- allow CS to reference a consistent “what kind of incident is this?” label without over-sharing internal root cause details

This ticket defines:
1) What we will surface in Console ops-only views (internal)
2) What subset (if any) can be made visible to CS in Console (or a CS-safe view) and what must stay restricted
3) The minimum permission model + audit expectations

## Goals
- Make incident type/subtype + resolved owner visible and filterable in ops Console incident views.
- Make it easy for on-call/IC to confirm classification + ownership without leaving Console.
- Provide CS with a CS-safe view of incident classification (where appropriate) to standardize customer comms.
- Avoid leaking sensitive internal implementation details (routing policy config, region capacity constraints, security-related signals).

## Non-goals
- Building a customer-facing “incident type” feature for end customers (status page / customer console) in this phase.
- Replacing incident-bot; Console is a consumer of the canonical fields.
- Deep RCA tooling; postmortems remain the source of truth for root cause narrative.

## Proposed UX scope
### A) Ops-only (internal) incident views
Add to:
- Incidents list view (ops)
- Incident detail view (ops)

Fields:
- Incident Type (required)
- Incident Subtype (required)
- Primary Owner Team (resolved from owner mapping config)
- Secondary/Consulted Teams (if present in mapping)
- Escalation channel (Slack) and oncall rotation name (if present / available)
- Runbook links (0–3 suggestions based on type/subtype)

Behaviors:
- Filtering + grouping by incident type, subtype, owner team
- Show “Unknown / Unclassified” bucket explicitly (but highlight as policy violation if incident is in an active state)
- Display “source of truth” indicator for owner resolution (e.g., “resolved from vX of owner-mapping config”) for auditability

### B) CS visibility (restricted)
We need a CS-safe subset that helps comms without prompting speculation:

CS-visible (proposed):
- Incident Type (top-level category only; no subtype unless explicitly approved)
- Customer-impact flag + current status (Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved)
- Owner contact path (CS escalation channel or on-call liaison), NOT internal team channels if they are noisy / contain sensitive info

CS-hidden (proposed):
- Subtype (often too specific and can imply root cause prematurely)
- Internal-only categories that overlap with security investigations
- Region/fleet constraints details, routing policies, or fallback reasons (unless curated comms snippet exists)

We should align “CS-visible” with the CS escalation playbook and comms templates being drafted.

## Data + API requirements
- Console API must return:
  - `incident_type`
  - `incident_subtype`
  - `resolved_owner_team`
  - `resolved_owner_channel`
  - `runbook_links`
  - `owner_mapping_version` (or similar)
- Console should not allow editing these fields in v1 (read-only). Editing happens via incident-bot to keep audit trail consistent.

## Permissions / RBAC
- Ops-only view: existing `ops` permission gate.
- CS view: allow read-only access to approved fields.
  - If we don’t have field-level RBAC available, we need either:
    1) separate endpoint for CS-safe payload
    2) separate “CS incident view” route backed by CS-safe response

Audit expectations:
- Access to incident classification fields should be logged for CS role (who viewed + when) to support enterprise escalation reviews.

## Copy / comms constraints
- When shown to CS, incident type must be framed as “classification for routing and reporting,” not “confirmed root cause.”
- UI should include small tooltip/inline copy: “Classification may update as investigation continues.”

## Dependencies / related work
- ENG-4825: owner mapping config and audit
- ENG-4822: incident-bot required fields + owner resolution
- DES-441: ops dashboard filters for incident type/owner
- PRs in flight:
  - redwood/pr-28503-expose-incident-type-in-ops-console-api (expected to provide core fields)

## Acceptance criteria
1) Ops Console incident list shows incident_type, incident_subtype, resolved_owner_team and supports filtering.
2) Incident detail page shows the above + links (runbooks, escalation channel) and owner mapping version.
3) CS role can view a CS-safe subset without seeing subtype or sensitive/internal-only details.
4) No PII or security-sensitive fields are exposed through Console APIs to CS role.
5) Instrumentation: basic analytics event for “incident detail viewed” with role and incident_type (low-cardinality) for adoption tracking.

## Open questions
- Do we have a canonical allowlist of “CS-safe incident types” vs “ops-only” types? If not, we need one (likely in the owner mapping config or separate policy file).
- Are there incident types that should be hidden from CS entirely (e.g., anything dual-tracked with Security Ops)?
- Field-level RBAC: do we implement a CS-safe endpoint, or can the platform support field-level filtering based on role?

## Rollout plan
- Phase 1: ops-only exposure (internal) behind feature flag `console.incidentTaxonomyOps`.
- Phase 2: CS-safe view behind `console.incidentTaxonomyCS` and limited to CS pilot group.
- Phase 3: remove flags after 2 weeks with no regressions; update CS onboarding docs.

## Links
- Confluence: Incident taxonomy + ownership program materials (taxonomy definitions, ownership mapping, dashboard spec)
- Design: DES-441
- Engineering: ENG-4822 / ENG-4825

## Notes / updates
- 2026-01-12 (Rachel Kim): CS request is not to see subtype; they want a stable top-level label they can reference in emails and post-incident reviews.
- 2026-01-20 (Nikhil Sharma): Met with Platform/Console; current RBAC model is route-based, not field-based. Leaning toward a CS-safe endpoint to avoid accidental leakage.
- 2026-02-02 (Nikhil Sharma): Dedicated stakeholders want CS to see the owning team contact path for fast escalations, but not the internal on-call channel; propose a dedicated “#cs-incident-escalations” handoff channel per tier.
- 2026-02-14 (Nikhil Sharma): Security Ops asked that anything involving auth anomalies should not automatically be surfaced to CS as “Auth/RBAC failure” until confirmed; prefer broader “Access/Authentication” label if shown at all and only when IC marks customer-impacting.
- 2026-02-21 (Nikhil Sharma): Sync with Design: add tooltip text and a subtle badge for “classification updated” to prevent CS over-indexing on early labels.
comments: 2026-01-20 — Mina Haddad (Routing): If Console shows subtype, please ensure it doesn’t include raw fallback reasons (capacity/health/policy/timeout) until the mapping is finalized. Those can be misread as root cause.
2026-01-23 — Allison Grant (Observability): For adoption tracking, keep analytics/event labels to top-level incident_type only. Subtype is too high-cardinality for dashboards and event pipelines.
2026-02-05 — Dev Patel (Support): CS needs a stable label + who to contact. We do NOT want CS to edit incident_type; we only need read-only and ideally a link to the comms snippet template per type.
2026-02-18 — Ethan Park (Control Plane): Owner mapping versioning is available; we can expose mapping version string (e.g., `owner_map:v7`) in the API for auditability.
